rules.title: It renews on its own
rules.plain: You'll keep getting charged every period until you actively cancel. Set a reminder if you only want it for a while.
rules.ask: When exactly does it renew, and how do I turn auto-renew off?

rules.title: You have to cancel early
rules.plain: Cancelling isn't instant — you must give notice a set number of days before renewal, or you're charged for another round.
rules.ask: How many days' notice do I need to cancel, and how do I give it (online, email, in writing)?

rules.title: You can cancel anytime
rules.plain: No lock-in: you can stop whenever you want (usually it ends at the close of the current billing period).

rules.title: They can raise the price
rules.plain: The price isn't locked. They're allowed to change what you pay, sometimes with only a short notice.
rules.ask: Is my price locked in? How much notice do I get before an increase, and can I cancel without penalty if it goes up?

rules.title: No refunds
rules.plain: Once you pay, you're unlikely to get money back — even if you cancel partway through.
rules.ask: If I cancel early or I'm unhappy, do I get any of my money back?

rules.title: There's a refund path
rules.plain: The terms mention refunds, a money-back guarantee, or a cooling-off period. Check the conditions and deadline.

rules.title: It costs money to leave
rules.plain: Ending the contract early triggers a fee or makes you pay out the rest of the term.
rules.ask: What exactly would I owe if I end this early?

rules.title: Free trial turns into paid
rules.plain: When the trial ends you're switched to a paid plan automatically unless you cancel before it finishes.
rules.ask: What day does the trial end, and will I get a reminder before I'm charged?

rules.title: Extra fees may apply
rules.plain: Beyond the headline price, there can be service, processing, admin, late or other fees. Budget for the real total.
rules.ask: What's the full price with every fee and tax included?

rules.title: They keep your card on file
rules.plain: You're giving them permission to charge your payment method again in the future without asking each time.

rules.title: You can't take them to court
rules.plain: Disputes go to a private arbitrator instead of a judge. It's usually faster but more favorable to companies, and you can't appeal much.
rules.ask: Can I opt out of arbitration, and how?

rules.title: No joining a class action
rules.plain: If they wrong lots of people, you can't team up with them in a group lawsuit — you'd have to go it alone.

rules.title: You give up a jury trial
rules.plain: Even if a case does go to court, you agree a judge alone decides it.

rules.title: You can opt out of arbitration
rules.plain: There's a window (often 30 days) to opt out of forced arbitration. Do it early if you want to keep your right to sue.

rules.title: Small claims court is allowed
rules.plain: You can still bring small disputes to small claims court — cheap and you don't need a lawyer.

rules.title: Your legal consumer rights still apply
rules.plain: The terms admit they can't override consumer protection laws where you live.

rules.title: They can change the rules anytime
rules.plain: They can rewrite these terms later, and simply continuing to use the service counts as agreeing to the new version.
rules.ask: How will I be told about changes, and can I leave without penalty if I don't agree?

rules.title: You'll be warned before changes
rules.plain: They commit to notifying you ahead of time before important changes kick in.
patterns: (notify|notice to|tell|inform) you (in advance|before|at least \d+ days|prior to)

rules.title: They can shut your account
rules.plain: They can suspend or close your account on their own call, sometimes without warning — and you may lose what's in it.

rules.title: Their responsibility is capped
rules.plain: If something goes wrong, the most they'll pay you is limited — often just what you paid them, or a small fixed amount.

rules.title: You cover their legal costs
rules.plain: If someone sues them because of something you did, you agree to pay their legal bills and damages.
rules.ask: What situations would make me responsible for their legal costs?

rules.title: No promises it works
rules.plain: The product is provided 'as is' — they don't guarantee it'll be reliable, accurate, or available.

rules.title: Disputes happen on their turf
rules.plain: The contract picks which country or state's laws apply and where cases are heard — which may be far from you.
patterns: governed by (and construed in accordance with )?the laws? of

rules.title: Your data gets shared
rules.plain: Your personal information can be shared with or sold to other companies like partners, affiliates or advertisers.
rules.ask: Who exactly gets my data, and can I opt out of sharing or selling it?

rules.title: You're tracked for ads
rules.plain: They use cookies or similar tech to follow what you do and show you targeted ads.

rules.title: They can use your stuff
rules.plain: Anything you upload or post, they get a broad (often worldwide, free, forever) right to use, copy and share it.
rules.ask: What can they do with the content I upload, and does that stop if I delete it?

rules.title: Your data may train their AI
rules.plain: What you share might be used to build or improve their algorithms or AI models.

rules.title: They may look at your activity
rules.plain: They reserve the right to monitor, record or review your messages, calls or content.

rules.title: They keep your data
rules.plain: Your information can be kept for a while — even after you close your account.

rules.title: You can get or delete your data
rules.plain: You have the right to access, download, correct or delete your information.

rules.title: Expect marketing messages
rules.plain: By agreeing you may be signing up for promotional emails, texts or calls. Look for an unsubscribe option.

rules.title: You're locked in
rules.plain: There's a minimum period you must stay (and pay) for, even if you want out earlier.
rules.ask: What's the minimum commitment, and what happens if I need to leave before it ends?

rules.title: You're personally on the hook
rules.plain: You personally guarantee the payments — your own money is at risk, not just a business's.

rules.title: It limits what you can do next
rules.plain: There are restrictions on working for competitors, starting a similar business, or poaching clients/staff.
rules.ask: How long and how wide are the non-compete or non-solicit restrictions?
patterns: shall not (directly or indirectly )?(compete|solicit|engage in any business)

rules.title: They can hand the contract to someone else
rules.plain: They may transfer this agreement to another company (e.g. if they're bought) — you might not be able to do the same.

rules.title: Money held as a deposit
rules.plain: There's a deposit or security amount. Check exactly when and how you get it back.
rules.ask: Under what conditions is the deposit returned, and how quickly?

rules.title: There's an age requirement
rules.plain: You must be a certain age (or have a parent's permission) to use this.
patterns: (at least|must be|over|under) (the age of )?(13|16|18|21|thirteen|sixteen|eighteen)( years)?( of age| old)?

rules.title: Unpaid bills go to collections
rules.plain: If you don't pay, they can hand your debt to a collection agency and charge you their costs.
rules.ask: When would they send my account to collections?

rules.title: Currency conversion fees
rules.plain: Paying in another currency can add conversion or foreign-transaction fees.

rules.title: Taxes on top
rules.plain: Prices shown may not include tax, so you'll pay more at checkout.

rules.title: Price is locked in
rules.plain: They promise not to raise your price for a set time.

rules.title: Disputing a charge can get you punished
rules.plain: If you ask your bank to reverse a charge, they may suspend your account or charge fees.
rules.ask: What happens if I dispute a charge with my bank?

rules.title: Prepaid money won't come back
rules.plain: Credits, balances or prepaid amounts can't be cashed out or refunded.

rules.title: Credits or points expire
rules.plain: Points, credits or balances vanish after a while if you don't use them.

rules.title: There's a minimum to spend
rules.plain: You may need to spend or order a minimum amount, or pay a fee if you don't.

rules.title: Fees if you don't use it
rules.plain: Leave the account idle and they start charging you.
rules.ask: Is there a fee if I stop using it for a while?

rules.title: Where your tips go
rules.plain: Check how tips are handled; some platforms keep part or use them to cover pay.

rules.title: Deductions from your deposit
rules.plain: They can keep part of your deposit for damage, cleaning or unpaid amounts.
rules.ask: What exactly can they deduct from my deposit, and when do I get it back?

rules.title: They'll match prices
rules.plain: If you find it cheaper, they'll match or refund the difference.

rules.title: Pay-later plan rules
rules.plain: Paying in installments may come with fees, interest or credit checks.
rules.ask: What happens if I miss an installment?

rules.title: Interest charges
rules.plain: Borrowed or financed amounts collect interest, which can add up quickly.
rules.ask: What's the APR and can it change?

rules.title: Intro price, then it goes up
rules.plain: The low price is only for the first period; after that you pay the regular rate.
rules.ask: What will I pay after the intro price ends?

rules.title: They can move you to a pricier plan
rules.plain: Go over your limit and they may bump you up a plan or bill overages.

rules.title: Refunds as store credit only
rules.plain: You may get credit to spend with them instead of your money back.

rules.title: Returns cost a restocking fee
rules.plain: Send something back and they keep part of the price.
rules.ask: How much does a return cost me?

rules.title: Cooling-off period
rules.plain: You get a short window to change your mind and cancel for a full refund.

rules.title: You give up legal rights
rules.plain: You agree to waive rights you'd normally have by law.
rules.ask: Which rights am I waiving exactly?

rules.title: Short deadline to make a claim
rules.plain: You only have a short time to bring a claim, after which you lose the right.
rules.ask: How long do I have to raise a problem?

rules.title: Limits on bad reviews
rules.plain: They try to stop you from posting negative reviews or comments.

rules.title: Disputes handled far away
rules.plain: Any legal fight happens under another place's laws or courts, which can be costly for you.
patterns: governed by the laws of (the state of |the )?(delaware|california|new york|england|ireland|singapore|luxembourg|the netherlands)

rules.title: They can remove your stuff
rules.plain: Your posts, files or listings can be removed at their discretion.
patterns: (remove|delete|take down) (any )?(content|listings?|posts?|materials?) (at any time|for any reason|in our (sole )?discretion|without notice)

rules.title: You may lose what you bought
rules.plain: If your account closes, you can lose access to purchases, games, music or credits.
rules.ask: What happens to what I bought if my account is closed?

rules.title: You're renting, not owning
rules.plain: Digital things you 'buy' are a licence to use, which they can limit or take back.

rules.title: You can't resell or transfer
rules.plain: Tickets, accounts or items can't be resold or given to someone else.

rules.title: Limited support promises
rules.plain: They don't promise any level of support or response time.

rules.title: No promise it'll work
rules.plain: They don't guarantee the service will be available, fast or error-free.

rules.title: Credits when it goes down
rules.plain: If the service is down too long, you get credit back.

rules.title: There's a warranty
rules.plain: Faulty products are covered for a set time.

rules.title: Easy ways to void the warranty
rules.plain: Opening, repairing or modifying it yourself can void the warranty.

rules.title: Repairs only through them
rules.plain: You must use their repair service or parts, or lose coverage.

rules.title: Other companies' rules apply too
rules.plain: Using parts of the service means agreeing to other companies' terms as well.

rules.title: Safety and emergency info
rules.plain: They explain what to do in an emergency or how they handle safety issues.

rules.title: Accessibility commitment
rules.plain: They commit to making the service usable for people with disabilities.

rules.title: Rules for kids
rules.plain: Children need a parent's permission or can't use it at all.

rules.title: You can appeal decisions
rules.plain: If they remove content or ban you, there's a way to appeal.

rules.title: Set penalties in advance
rules.plain: The contract names fixed amounts you'll owe if you break it, whatever the real cost.
rules.ask: How much would I owe if I broke this early?

rules.title: You might pay their lawyers
rules.plain: If there's a legal fight, you could be on the hook for their legal costs.
rules.ask: Who pays legal costs if there's a dispute?

rules.title: Face, voice or fingerprint data
rules.plain: They collect biometric data like face scans, voiceprints or fingerprints.
rules.ask: How is my biometric data stored and when is it deleted?

rules.title: They track where you are
rules.plain: They collect your precise location, sometimes even in the background.
patterns: location (data|information) (even )?when (the app is )?(closed|not in use|in the background)
rules.ask: Can I use it without sharing my location?

rules.title: Health information
rules.plain: They collect health or medical details, which are very sensitive.
rules.ask: Who can see my health information?

rules.title: They read your contacts
rules.plain: The app may upload your phone contacts or address book.

rules.title: They link your devices
rules.plain: They connect your activity across phones, laptops and other devices.

rules.title: Data from brokers
rules.plain: They buy extra information about you from data brokers or other sources.

rules.title: Your data goes abroad
rules.plain: Your information may be stored or processed in other countries with different protections.

rules.title: They'll tell you about breaches
rules.plain: If your data is exposed, they commit to letting you know.

rules.title: Camera and microphone access
rules.plain: The app asks to use your camera or microphone.

rules.title: Children's data
rules.plain: They explain how they handle information from kids.

rules.title: 'Anonymous' data is theirs to use
rules.plain: Data with your name removed can be used or sold freely, and isn't always truly anonymous.

rules.title: Sensitive personal details
rules.plain: They may collect sensitive details like race, religion, sexual orientation or finances.

rules.title: They may check your credit
rules.plain: They can run a credit check, which may show up on your credit file.
rules.ask: Is it a soft or hard credit check?

rules.title: Cancelling is a hassle
rules.plain: You can't just cancel online; you must call, write, or go in person.
rules.ask: Can I cancel online?

rules.title: Repeat deliveries
rules.plain: You'll get regular shipments and charges until you stop them.
rules.ask: How do I skip or stop deliveries?

rules.title: You can't use competitors
rules.plain: You agree to only use them, or not to work with competitors.

rules.title: They own what you create
rules.plain: Work you make while under this agreement belongs to them.
rules.ask: Do I keep anything I create on my own time?

rules.title: You must keep things secret
rules.plain: You agree to keep certain information confidential, sometimes for years.

rules.title: You can't poach their people
rules.plain: After leaving, you can't recruit their staff or approach their clients.

rules.title: Probation period
rules.plain: There's a trial period where you can be let go more easily.

rules.title: Extra hours may be unpaid
rules.plain: You may be expected to work extra hours without extra pay.

rules.title: They can take money back
rules.plain: Bonuses, commissions or relocation money must be paid back in some cases.
rules.ask: When would I have to pay money back?

rules.title: You're responsible for guests
rules.plain: You're on the hook for anything your guests, kids or other users do.

rules.title: Rent can go up
rules.plain: They explain when and by how much rent can be raised.
rules.ask: How often and by how much can rent go up?

rules.title: Repairs fall on you
rules.plain: You may have to pay for repairs or upkeep yourself.

rules.title: No subletting without OK
rules.plain: You can't rent out the place or share it without permission.

rules.title: Rules for pets
rules.plain: There are rules, fees or bans for pets.

rules.title: You must have insurance
rules.plain: You're required to carry your own insurance.

rules.title: You pay the first part
rules.plain: In a claim, you pay a set amount (the excess or deductible) before they pay.
rules.ask: How much is the excess or deductible?

rules.title: Things that aren't covered
rules.plain: There's a list of situations they won't cover, so check it carefully.
rules.ask: What are the biggest things that aren't covered?

rules.title: Pre-existing conditions excluded
rules.plain: Problems you already had before signing up may not be covered.

rules.title: Waiting period before cover
rules.plain: You have to wait a while before you're covered or can claim.

rules.title: You pay for damage
rules.plain: If the car, bike or item is damaged while you have it, you pay.
rules.ask: What would damage cost me, and is there cover?

rules.title: Cancel late, pay anyway
rules.plain: Cancel a booking too close to the date and you lose money.
rules.ask: Until when can I cancel for free?

rules.title: Virtual coins have no real value
rules.plain: In-game coins or tokens aren't real money and can be changed or removed.

rules.title: Random paid rewards
rules.plain: Some purchases give random items, so you might not get what you want.

rules.title: Strict anti-cheat bans
rules.plain: Using mods, cheats or third-party tools can get you banned permanently.

rules.title: Allergens aren't guaranteed
rules.plain: They can't promise food is free from allergens, so take care if you have allergies.

rules.title: Rules for missing or wrong orders
rules.plain: There are limits on how and when you can report a missing or wrong order.
rules.ask: How quickly do I need to report a problem with an order?

rules.title: Do a patch test
rules.plain: They recommend testing products on your skin first and won't be responsible for reactions.

rules.title: Opened items can't be returned
rules.plain: Once a product is opened or used, you usually can't send it back.
patterns: (opened|used|unsealed|worn) (products?|items?|goods) (cannot|can't|may not|are not eligible to) be returned

rules.title: Results aren't promised
rules.plain: They don't guarantee the product or service will work for you.

rules.title: Not medical or professional advice
rules.plain: The info is general and not a replacement for a doctor or professional.

rules.title: You can lose money
rules.plain: Investing or trading carries risk, and you could lose some or all of your money.

rules.title: Your money isn't protected
rules.plain: Balances may not be covered by deposit insurance if the company fails.

rules.title: Limits on taking your money out
rules.plain: There are limits, delays or fees on withdrawing your money.
rules.ask: How fast can I take my money out?

rules.title: They can hold your money
rules.plain: They can freeze or hold your funds or payouts, sometimes for months.

rules.title: Delivery dates aren't promises
rules.plain: Delivery times are estimates, and delays usually don't earn you anything.

rules.title: Lost in the post may be your problem
rules.plain: Once the item ships, it may be your risk if it's lost or damaged.

rules.title: In-app purchases
rules.plain: The app sells extras inside it, which can add up.

rules.title: AI answers can be wrong
rules.plain: The service uses AI, and its answers can be wrong; you're responsible for checking them.

rules.title: Test features may break
rules.plain: Beta or preview features may change, break or disappear.

rules.title: Updates install on their own
rules.plain: The app or device updates itself, which can change or remove features.

rules.title: Locked to their network or device
rules.plain: The device or service is locked to them until conditions are met.

rules.title: You can pause it
rules.plain: You can freeze or pause your membership instead of cancelling.

rules.title: Cancel online
rules.plain: You can cancel yourself online or in the app.
patterns: cancel (at any time )?(online|in (the )?app|through (your )?account settings|from your account)

rules.title: Pro-rated refunds
rules.plain: If you cancel mid-period you get back money for the unused part.

rules.title: A real person can review it
rules.plain: You can ask for a human to review automated decisions about you.

rules.title: Free outside help with complaints
rules.plain: You can take complaints to an independent ombudsman or regulator for free.

rules.title: Opt out of data sale
rules.plain: There's a way to tell them not to sell or share your data.
